summary: Independently verified .1R.5.2's F1 repair (verifier-owned identity registry closing the object.__new__ trusted-construction bypass HPAC-REQ-056 requires closed). Independently re-derived HPAC-REQ-056/057/058 directly from docs/contracts/HUMAN_PRINCIPAL_AUTHENTICATION_CONTRACT.md §19 before re-reading .1R.5.2's own prose, then independently re-executed every attack in the governing prompt's checklist against current src/pcae/core/hpac_verifier.py, not trusting .1R.5.2's report or its own test suite as an oracle: object.__new__ forgery (isinstance remains unavoidably True -- a Python-language fact, not a defect any construction-boundary fix could close -- but is_verifier_authenticated_principal correctly returns False), direct construction without the seal (rejected at __init__, defense-in-depth), direct construction WITH the real module-private seal obtained via import (construction succeeds but the result is still never registered, proving the seal is not the trust boundary), shallow copy/deepcopy/pickle of a legitimate result (all TypeError via __reduce__, unchanged), manual __slots__ state cloning and reflection-based reconstruction (type(x).__new__(type(x)) + setattr per slot) of a legitimate result (never registry members), subclassing (refused at class-definition time via __init_subclass__), equality/hash-collision (id-based hash/eq, no collision possible by construction), object-ID reuse after del+gc.collect() (foreclosed because the registry holds strong references, so a registered object is never actually freed while registered), and process-restart-proxy semantics via importlib.reload (run in an isolated subprocess to avoid contaminating this phase's own shared pytest session -- a test-isolation bug caught and fixed during this phase's own draft, disclosed in the report rather than hidden). Every attack HPAC-REQ-056 requires to fail, fails. The one attack that succeeds -- same-process direct mutation of the importable module-level _AUTHENTIC_PRINCIPAL_REGISTRY object via `from pcae.core.hpac_verifier import _AUTHENTIC_PRINCIPAL_REGISTRY; _AUTHENTIC_PRINCIPAL_REGISTRY.add(forged)` -- is independently analyzed as outside HPAC-REQ-056's own textual scope (the requirement is about construction 'from caller-supplied strings or dicts', not about resistance to an attacker who already possesses independent same-process code-execution capability sufficient to import and rewrite the verifier module's own internals -- a limitation B1's own identical-pattern identity-registry repair, 149O.20L.7O.3W.1R.2 §9, already shares and does not claim to close either). Disclosed as new observation F7, not hidden and not treated as a regression. F1: CLOSED. F2 (HPAC-REQ-054 step 4 recomputation gap), F3 (.1R.4 planning-doc 'eight-step' debt), F4 (pre-existing test-name overclaim in test_hpac_verifier.py) independently re-confirmed unchanged this phase -- git diff befd7a5a..de7ef732 -- src/pcae/core/hpac_verifier.py shows zero lines touching the step-3/4 resolution logic, confirming F2/F3 could not have been affected; none self-closed. Added tests/test_hpac_verifier_repair_independent_verification_3w1r2b1r1115a21.py (29 new tests, independently derived from the contract text and this phase's own attack checklist, not copied from .1R.5.2's own new suite -- only the _Rig fixture harness from tests/test_hpac_verifier.py is reused, for fixture setup only). Full 21-file HPAC-family regression sweep (the same 20 files .1R.5.2 §14.1 used, plus this phase's own new file): 458 passed / 54 failed -- an exact arithmetic match to .1R.5.2's own disclosed 429-pass candidate-state count plus this phase's 29 new passing tests, with the 54 failures matching .1R.5.2's own disclosed pre-existing/unrelated failure set by test ID (independently re-run, not assumed). Zero unexplained attributable regressions. No production source file modified this phase (verification-only: new test file + this phase's report). No B1/B7/N1/N2 repair; no PB/runtime-authority integration; no real FIDO2/UI; execution not enabled. Final verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- VERIFIER IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE. Next canonical phase not invented; requires separate explicit human authorization and phase-ID confirmation.
